1. Exchange rate (core). Every trim lands on one frontier of about 0.07–0.1 pp per 0.1 s:
   - E033, E037, E040, E041 and E039 on its rate.
   - E031 is only slightly better, within noise.
   - My mechanism: accuracy tracks the total useful update signal (steps × the share of the network those steps reach). Low resolution, frozen layers and dropped samples are cheap because they deliver less signal. Only pure overhead (launches, memory traffic with no gradient, prepare) sits off the frontier.
2. E042 miss. Staggered conv1 freeze at 60% scored 0.7549 on seeds 0–2 for −0.05 s, above my range, yet it was discarded. I read it as seed luck on a small, near-free cut. Conv1 wgrad and the pool backward at 31×31 are cheap (~1.5 ms/step) and carry little signal, which fits the frontier.
3. Noise:
   - Seeds 0–2 SD ≈ 0.15 pp; 10-seed SD ≈ 0.08 pp.
   - Winner's curse on seeds 3–12 ≈ 0.1–0.2 pp (E038).
   - Math-identical rebuilds re-roll per-seed results (E035 moved +0.09 pp).
   - Time is reproducible to ±0.02 s.
4. Stem truncation is bandwidth-heavy, ~7 ms per truncated step. Group 2 is compute-bound: freezing it saves ~8 ms/step but costs real signal, because group 2 is the main feature block.
5. End-of-run calibration is the one untested non-trajectory lever.
   - The final Lookahead copy lerps the BN buffers. The weights are averaged, but the stats were gathered on fast weights at BN momentum 0.4.
   - Recalibration on a few 32 px batches should give a small, positive, low-variance gain (+0.05–0.15 pp), measured cleanly by the paired design.
   - Of the remaining ideas, it is the most likely to clear the gate cheaply (+0.02–0.04 s).
6. Batch/steps (H5). Halving the batch at 20 px doubles the step count in the cheapest phase, but each step pays fixed overhead: the Python loop, Muon NS on all filters, the optimizer and Lookahead. That is ~3–4 ms × 69 extra steps ≈ +0.25 s. Accuracy gain is uncertain (+0–0.3 pp), so it probably lands on or slightly off the frontier.
7. Systems:
   - Cin=24 padding is likely neutral. cuDNN already pads channels_last fp16 internally, and widening the whitening output adds 33% of GELU traffic at 31×31.
   - Conv1 is ~6% of MACs. I expect it to take 8–12% of step time.
   - Non-GEMM work is probably ≥30% of the step.
8. Strategy. Pair BN recalibration (+~0.1 pp) with one frontier cut (~−0.1 s) or a pure-overhead cut. Realistic floor is ~5.15–5.25 s at a population mean ≈0.753.

W5 (contrarian), after E042. The tip is still E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0–2, 0.7525 on fresh seeds 13–22. The population mean is about 0.7525, so the 3-seed gate of 0.753 is basically a coin flip for any change that leaves accuracy alone.

1. Exchange rate (core). Every trim lands on one frontier of about 0.07–0.1 pp per 0.1 s:
   - E033, E037, E040, E041 and E039 on its rate.
   - E031 is only slightly better, within noise.
   - My mechanism: accuracy tracks the total useful update signal (steps × the share of the network those steps reach). Low resolution, frozen layers and dropped samples are cheap because they deliver less signal. Only pure overhead (launches, memory traffic with no gradient, prepare) sits off the frontier.
2. E042 miss. Staggered conv1 freeze at 60% scored 0.7549 on seeds 0–2 for −0.05 s, above my range, yet it was discarded. I read it as seed luck on a small, near-free cut. Conv1 wgrad and the pool backward at 31×31 are cheap (~1.5 ms/step) and carry little signal, which fits the frontier.
3. Noise:
   - Seeds 0–2 SD ≈ 0.15 pp; 10-seed SD ≈ 0.08 pp.
   - Winner's curse on seeds 3–12 ≈ 0.1–0.2 pp (E038).
   - Math-identical rebuilds re-roll per-seed results (E035 moved +0.09 pp).
   - Time is reproducible to ±0.02 s.
4. Stem truncation is bandwidth-heavy, ~7 ms per truncated step. Group 2 is compute-bound: freezing it saves ~8 ms/step but costs real signal, because group 2 is the main feature block.
5. End-of-run calibration is the one untested non-trajectory lever.
   - The final Lookahead copy lerps the BN buffers. The weights are averaged, but the stats were gathered on fast weights at BN momentum 0.4.
   - Recalibration on a few 32 px batches should give a small, positive, low-variance gain (+0.05–0.15 pp), measured cleanly by the paired design.
   - Of the remaining ideas, it is the most likely to clear the gate cheaply (+0.02–0.04 s).
6. Batch/steps (H5). Halving the batch at 20 px doubles the step count in the cheapest phase, but each step pays fixed overhead: the Python loop, Muon NS on all filters, the optimizer and Lookahead. That is ~3–4 ms × 69 extra steps ≈ +0.25 s. Accuracy gain is uncertain (+0–0.3 pp), so it probably lands on or slightly off the frontier.
7. Systems:
   - Cin=24 padding is likely neutral. cuDNN already pads channels_last fp16 internally, and widening the whitening output adds 33% of GELU traffic at 31×31.
   - Conv1 is ~6% of MACs. I expect it to take 8–12% of step time.
   - Non-GEMM work is probably ≥30% of the step.
8. Strategy. Pair BN recalibration (+~0.1 pp) with one frontier cut (~−0.1 s) or a pure-overhead cut. Realistic floor is ~5.15–5.25 s at a population mean ≈0.753.

Unsure: the size of the PCIe transfer discount on bandwidth-bound levers; whether small batches help under Muon; whether recalibration hurts (stats from augmented train-mode batches vs the clean test distribution).

forecasts.reason: Final BN stats are lerped buffers from fast weights. Recalibration should give a small positive paired gain of ~+0.1 pp, near the 0.15 pp threshold, for +0.02–0.05 s.
About 69 extra steps each pay fixed Muon, optimizer and launch overhead (~+0.25 s). The accuracy gain from more steps is plausible but small, so it ends up on the frontier.
Group-2 backward is compute-bound signal, not overhead. Saving ~0.17 s costs ~0.15–0.2 pp, on the frontier and above the 0.1 pp allowance.
Diagnostic. Conv1 is likely inefficient but ~8–12% of the step. The 'less than half TFLOP/s and ≥10%' test is close to a coin flip.
A 5% sample drop gives about 4% time savings, and the accuracy cost on the dial rate is ~0.13 pp, more than the 0.1 pp allowance.
cuDNN already pads Cin internally, and the 32-channel whitening output adds elementwise traffic at 31×31, so the time change should be under 2%.

cruxes: Does BN recalibration after the final Lookahead copy give a paired gain of ≥0.1 pp on seeds 13–32? If so, it funds one frontier cut and is the cheapest path below 5.3 s.

What fraction of a train() call is per-step fixed overhead (Python loop, Muon NS, optimizer, Lookahead, launches) versus convolution compute? This decides whether small-batch ideas (I068) or step-removal ideas are the better lever.
Is any lever off the ~0.08 pp per 0.1 s frontier other than pure overhead? E042's 0.7549 needs fresh-seed confirmation before I believe the conv1 freeze is free.
